title: Mapping spaces between arrows retain a coherent compatibility path
statement:
Use quasicategories, internal functor categories and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal D$ be any quasicategory and put $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal D)=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal D)$. For objects $u:d_0\to d_1$ and $v:e_0\to e_1$ of $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal D)$, there is a natural equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal D)}(u,v)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(d_0,e_0)\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(d_0,e_1)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(d_1,e_1).$$
Here the two maps to the base send $a$ to $va$ and $b$ to $bu$. For maps $f:X\to Z$ and $g:Y\to Z$ of spaces, $X\times_Z^hY$ denotes the space of triples $(x,y,\gamma)$, where $\gamma$ is a path from $f(x)$ to $g(y)$, including all higher simplices; it is modeled by $X\times_{Z,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Z)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Z}Y$. The displayed equivalence is compatible, up to coherent homotopy, with the joint endpoint projection to $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(d_0,e_0)\times\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(d_1,e_1)$. It is natural in both arrows and in simplicial functors between quasicategories. Composition and the displayed maps of spaces are understood with their coherent homotopies.

source.place: Theorem 8.3.7.1 (Kerodon Tag 06BZ), applied to the oriented fiber product of the two identity functors of D, which is Arr(D); its Hom-functor square gives the joint endpoint projection. Right-pinched versus unpinched conventions are related by the existing lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison (Kerodon 01L5). Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags. Read online 2026-10-16; WANTED: archived source.

proof.text: Write $U(x,y)=\{x\}\times_{\mathcal D,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal D)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,\mathcal D}\{y\}$ and put $A=U(d_0,e_0)$, $B=U(d_1,e_1)$, $C=U(d_0,e_1)$. These are Kan complexes by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. The category $\mathcal Q=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal D)$ is a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-internal-hom-quasicategory]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] also to $\mathcal Q$: its right-pinched mapping space from $u$ to $v$ is naturally equivalent to $U_{\mathcal Q}(u,v)$. By the internal-functor formula in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], an $n$-simplex of this last space is a map $\Delta^1_s\times\Delta^1_t\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal D$ whose $t=0$ and $t=1$ restrictions are the constant families $u$ and $v$, respectively. Its $s=0$ and $s=1$ restrictions lie in $A$ and $B$.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10; internal functor definition, and Lecture II basic fact (1) for Q

proof.text: Use $H(x,y,z)$ for the space of maps $\Delta^2\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal D$ constant at $x,y,z$ on the three vertex families. Let $P_v\subseteq H(d_0,e_0,e_1)$ impose edge $12=v$, and let $Q_u\subseteq H(d_0,d_1,e_1)$ impose edge $01=u$, in each degree. Restriction to the other consecutive edge gives $r:P_v\to A$ and $s:Q_u\to B$. They are pullbacks of the $n=2$ spine restriction of [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine], so they lift every boundary inclusion: compose a lifting problem with the spine restriction, fill it, and keep the fixed edge. Thus they are trivial Kan fibrations and are homotopy equivalences by [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence]. Since $A,B$ are Kan, the model-structure characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] also makes $P_v,Q_u$ Kan. Write $p:P_v\to C$ and $q:Q_u\to C$ for restriction to edge $02$. The composition convention of [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine] represents postcomposition by $v$ by the span $A\xleftarrow{r}P_v\xrightarrow{p}C$, and precomposition by $u$ by $B\xleftarrow{s}Q_u\xrightarrow{q}C$.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.8.5 and Construction 4.6.8.9: fixed-leg pullbacks of the triangle spine map

proof.text: Both long-edge maps $p$ and $q$ are Kan fibrations. Here are the horn lifts, so that no fibration property is inferred from the spine map. For $p$ take $L=\Delta^{\{0,2\}}\cup\Delta^{\{1,2\}}\subseteq\Delta^2$, prescribing the long edge and $v$; for $q$ take $L=\Delta^{\{0,1\}}\cup\Delta^{\{0,2\}}$, prescribing $u$ and the long edge. In either case a horn lift is extension of a map on $(L\times\Delta^m)\cup(\Delta^2\times\Lambda_i^m)$, with all vertex families constant. For $0<i<m$, this inclusion is inner anodyne by [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product], applied to $L\hookrightarrow\Delta^2$ and the inner horn, and $\mathcal D\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration by its defining horn condition. For $i=0$, $m\geq2$, apply [lem-cbc-invertible-prism-extension]: every vertex-direction edge is an identity, hence an equivalence. For $i=m$, reverse the orders in both simplex coordinates and apply that same cited statement to $\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $L^{\mathrm{op}}\subseteq(\Delta^2)^{\mathrm{op}}$; order reversal interchanges the outer horns, preserves inner horns and preserves the inverse-triangle definition of equivalence. For $m=1$, the prescribed edge in $\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal D)$ is an equivalence by the componentwise criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], since every vertex component is an identity. The isofibration $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^2,\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal D)$ of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] lifts it from a specified source. To lift from a specified target, apply this isofibration statement to the opposite simplicial sets. Because $L$ contains all vertices and the prescribed fixed edge, these lifts stay in $P_v$ or $Q_u$ as required.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.8 for the outer prisms; agent-expanded long-edge horn lifting, using the cited exponential and inner pushout-product statements

proof.text: The simplicial square $\Delta^1_s\times\Delta^1_t$ is the union of the two triangles with vertex sequences $((0,0),(0,1),(1,1))$ and $((0,0),(1,0),(1,1))$, along their common edge $((0,0),(1,1))$. A map from this union is exactly two maps agreeing on that edge, in every degree and after every simplicial restriction. The boundary conditions $t=0:u$ and $t=1:v$ impose precisely the fixed edges defining $Q_u$ and $P_v$. Consequently the internal-functor definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] gives a strict isomorphism $U_{\mathcal Q}(u,v)=P_v\times_C Q_u$. Under it the joint endpoint map is $(r,s):P_v\times_C Q_u\to A\times B$.

source.place: Agent-expanded interval case: degreewise triangulation of the interval square; source theorem checks the resulting Hom square

proof.text: Since $p,q$ are Kan fibrations between Kan complexes, [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] identifies $P_v\times_C Q_u$ with the path homotopy pullback $P_v\times_C^h Q_u$. Choose simplicial sections $\sigma:A\to P_v$ and $\tau:B\to Q_u$ of the trivial fibrations $r,s$. They exist by boundary lifting against every monomorphism: the boundary-cell description in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] gives the requisite lift against $\varnothing\to A$ and $\varnothing\to B$. Since $r\sigma=1_A$ and $s\tau=1_B$, two-out-of-three makes $\sigma,\tau$ weak equivalences. The composition-span convention in [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine] makes $p\sigma$ and $q\tau$ actual representatives of $v\circ(-)$ and $(-)\circ u$. The maps $(\sigma,\operatorname{id}_C,\tau)$ form a strictly commuting map of Kan cospans from $A\xrightarrow{p\sigma}C\xleftarrow{q\tau}B$ to $P_v\xrightarrow{p}C\xleftarrow{q}Q_u$. By [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] their path pullbacks are weakly equivalent. The composite projection to $A\times B$ is the actual pair $(r,s)$, because $r\sigma$ and $s\tau$ are identities. Thus the identification retains the endpoint map and uses only strict-cospan invariance, without any coherent-localization theorem.

source.place: Construction 4.6.8.9, combined with the cited Kan homotopy-pullback replacement theorem; agent-expanded triangulation proof

proof.text: Model $A\times_C^h B$ by $A\times_{C,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,C}B$. The homotopy-fiber convention in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] makes its simplices triples $(a,b,\gamma)$ with a path $\gamma:va\simeq bu$ and all higher simplices. The natural pinch maps of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], for $\mathcal Q$ and for the three pairs of endpoints in $\mathcal D$, replace every $U$ by the specified right-pinched mapping space. Their compatibility with evaluation is explicit: restricting the simplicial map defining a pinch to $s=0$ or $s=1$ is the pinch of that endpoint restriction. Thus the resulting equivalence has exactly the joint endpoint projection in the statement. The two maps into the cross term use the coherent composition spans from step 2; no strict choice of composition is part of the assertion.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10; path model as defined in the statement and enhanced-diagram definition

proof.text: All maps before inversion are restrictions or postcomposition of simplicial maps; these commute with simplicial operators and any simplicial functor $\mathcal D\to\mathcal D'$. The spine statement [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine] supplies coherent composition in both $\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal Q$. Explicitly, if squares $u\to v$ and $v\to w$ have data $(a,b,\gamma:va\simeq bu)$ and $(a',b',\delta:wa'\simeq b'v)$, pasting them gives endpoint maps $a'a,b'b$ and the path obtained by concatenating $wa'a\xRightarrow{\delta\,a}b'va\xRightarrow{b'\gamma}b'bu$, with the composition associativity homotopies supplied by that cited spine statement. This is the square obtained by restricting a composable pair in $\mathcal Q$ to the two endpoints, since those restrictions are simplicial functors. The degenerate square gives the two identity endpoints and constant compatibility path. For any longer string, use the cited spine maps in $\mathcal Q$ and $\mathcal D$: their face restrictions give every parenthesization and their degeneracies give the identities, and the face/degeneracy identities give their higher compatibility. Inverting these trivial Kan equivalences preserves those diagrams of spaces. This verifies compatibility with composition and hence naturality under precomposition in the first arrow and postcomposition in the second, including all higher simplices. Together with the strict commutation with simplicial functors and the natural pinch maps from [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], it proves the claimed naturality.
